h1: The 6 Best Eightree Smart Plugs of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Eightree Smart Plugs: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 Eightree smart plugs scored on Wi-Fi band support, 15A rating, platform compatibility and energy monitoring.
summary: The Eightree 5GHz plug with energy monitoring is the one to buy for most homes: dual-band Wi-Fi, ETL and FCC listing, and a usage readout the others lack. The 5GHz 15A model is the plain workhorse, the SmartThings version is for Samsung households, and the outdoor plug covers holiday lights and pumps. The round mini is the pick when the outlet is crowded.
intro: Most smart plug trouble starts at the router, not the plug. A cheap plug that only joins the 2.4GHz band will drop offline the day you split your network, and the setup screen will never explain why. Eightree sells a range that mixes both kinds, so picking the right one inside the line matters more than picking the brand.

We ranked six Eightree models, reading each listing for Wi-Fi band support, current rating, certifications, voice platforms and physical size. Everything below is drawn from the specs the listings print. Where a model's page says nothing about a feature, we say so rather than guess, which is why the energy-monitoring plug leads and the round mini finishes last.

products.name: EIGHTREE 5GHz Smart Plug with Energy Monitoring
products.verdict: The only Eightree here that tracks energy use, and it joins both 5GHz and 2.4GHz networks.
products.description:
This 4-pack handles both 5GHz and 2.4GHz Wi-Fi, is ETL and FCC listed, works with Alexa and Google Home, and adds built-in energy monitoring. It is also sized so two plugs fit one duplex outlet.

Energy monitoring is what separates it. A plug that reports usage tells you which space heater, game console or chest freezer is actually running up the bill, which is the real reason most people buy smart plugs. The other Eightree models switch power on and off but cannot report it. Certification also counts: ETL listing means a recognized lab checked the plug against safety standards, a point the cheaper listings leave out.

Buy it for any appliance you want to schedule and measure. The limit is that the listing gives no amp rating, so confirm the load before plugging in a heater.
products.idealFor: Anyone who wants to see which appliances drive the power bill.
products.skipIf: You only need a plain on and off switch.

products.name: EIGHTREE 5GHz Smart Plug 15A
products.verdict: A 15A, 1800W dual-band plug with Bluetooth setup. The best plain plug in the line.
products.description:
This 4-pack is rated 120V and 15A (1800W), joins 5GHz and 2.4GHz networks, sets up over Bluetooth and works with Alexa and Google Home. It is the model to buy when you want a published load rating and no extras.

It ranks second because the 1800W figure is the one that matters for power-hungry gear. A plug rated below 15A can run hot with a space heater, and this listing states the full figure. It trails the energy-monitoring pick only in features, not hardware, and it beats the 2.4GHz-only mini and standard 4-pack because the dual-band radio means setup survives a router change. Bluetooth pairing also skips the fiddly hotspot step.

Buy it for lamps, fans and window units. It cannot report usage, so you will guess your savings.
products.idealFor: General household use with heavier loads like a window fan.

products.name: EIGHTREE 15A Smart Plug with SmartThings
products.verdict: The only Eightree that lists SmartThings next to Alexa and Google Home.
products.description:
This 4-pack carries a 15A rating, runs through the Smart Life app, needs no hub and works with Alexa, Google Home and SmartThings. It sits in the under $25 bucket, so it is also the cheapest way into the SmartThings ecosystem in this ranking.

The SmartThings link is why it ranks third. A Samsung household can fold the plugs into routines alongside lights and sensors without an extra bridge, which none of the other Eightree models list. It falls behind the 5GHz 15A because the listing does not state band support, so a 5GHz-only router is a risk. Without a band mention, assume 2.4GHz.

Buy it for a Samsung-centric home on a budget. If your router hides the 2.4GHz band, check compatibility before you buy.
cons: Relies on the Smart Life app
products.idealFor: Samsung SmartThings homes on a tight budget.

products.name: EIGHTREE Outdoor Smart Plug, 2 Independent Outlets
products.verdict: Two independently controlled outlets with IP44 splash protection and extended Wi-Fi range.
products.description:
This is the only Eightree plug built for outdoor use. It has two independent outlets, IP44 splash protection, a 15A rating and extended Wi-Fi range, and the listing positions it as a timer outlet for outdoor loads.

It ranks fourth because it solves a different problem than the others. Two outlets on separate switches mean string lights can run on one schedule and a pump or fountain on another. The IP44 rating covers splashes, not submersion, so it still needs a covered spot. Next to the SmartThings plug it costs the same bucket but does not list SmartThings or Bluetooth setup.

Buy it for holiday lights, patio lamps and small pumps. Keep it off a ground-level puddle zone, since IP44 is splash protection only.
products.idealFor: Outdoor holiday lights and pumps on separate schedules.

products.name: EIGHTREE Smart Plug WiFi Outlet, 15A, 4 Pack
products.verdict: A 15A plug sold in 1, 2 or 4 packs with Bluetooth auto-detect setup.
products.description:
This 15A Wi-Fi outlet runs on the Smart Life app, uses Bluetooth auto-detect for setup and works with Alexa and Google Home. It is sold in 1, 2 and 4 packs, so you can buy just what you need, which no other Eightree model offers.

It ranks fifth because the listing states neither the band nor an energy feature, and the 5GHz 15A model gives you more for the same bucket. Still, the single-pack option means you can test one plug on your network before buying four, and Bluetooth auto-detect speeds up pairing compared with the older hotspot method.

Buy it for a first smart plug or a small apartment. The weakness is the missing band specification, so verify your router before ordering a four-pack.
products.idealFor: First-time buyers who want to start with a single plug.

products.name: EIGHTREE 15A Smart Plug, Round Mini
products.verdict: A round plug just 1.2 inches thick. Easy to fit behind furniture, but 2.4GHz only.
products.description:
The Round Mini is a 15A, 1800W plug that sits 1.2 inches off the wall. It connects on 2.4GHz only, is set up over Bluetooth through the Smart Life app, needs no hub and comes in 2 or 4 packs.

Its thin shape is the reason to buy it. A slim plug lets a sofa or bed sit nearer the wall and leaves the second socket on a duplex outlet free. It ranks last because 2.4GHz-only operation is a real limit: it fails the day your router bands are merged or removed, and the dual-band models above avoid that trap.

Buy it for tight spots behind furniture where depth matters more than network flexibility. Check your router has a 2.4GHz network first.
cons: Setup relies on Smart Life app
products.idealFor: Outlets behind furniture where depth is the constraint.

methodology.title: Wi-Fi band support
methodology.description: Plugs that state both 5GHz and 2.4GHz scored higher, because a single-band plug can break on a router change.

methodology.title: Current rating and safety listing
methodology.description: We favored published 15A ratings and recognized certifications such as ETL, since heater and appliance loads are where cheap plugs fail.

methodology.title: Platform and app fit
methodology.description: Alexa, Google Home and SmartThings support were weighed against the Smart Life app that most of these plugs rely on.

methodology.title: Features that save money
methodology.description: Energy monitoring and independent outlets were credited because they change what you can do with the plug.

methodology.title: Physical fit
methodology.description: Thickness and outlet sharing were compared, since a bulky plug can block the second socket.

whatMatters.detail: Smart plugs connect over 2.4GHz, 5GHz or both. Many still speak only 2.4GHz, which breaks when a router merges or drops that band. A dual-band plug is more forgiving, because it will follow the router. Look for the band line in the specs, and treat silence on the listing as a warning, not a promise.

The amp rating tells you how much load the relay can switch. A 15A plug is rated for 1800W at 120V, enough for a heater or window air conditioner, while lower-rated plugs can overheat on the same load. Find the rating on the listing, then add up the wattage printed on your appliance and keep a margin.

ETL and FCC marks mean independent labs checked the plug for electrical safety and radio emissions. Without them, you are relying on the maker's word for a device that sits in a wall socket and switches mains power. Certification is stated on the energy-monitoring model, so read the listing for the logo and for the standard cited.

Several plugs here run on the Smart Life app, then bridge to Alexa, Google Home and in one case SmartThings. This matters because a routine only works on the platform you already use. Before buying, check which ecosystem runs your lights and speakers, and confirm it appears in the platform line, not just in marketing copy.

A wide plug covers both sockets on a duplex outlet, wasting the second one. The energy-monitoring model is sized so two plugs fit one outlet, and the Round Mini is only 1.2 inches thick. Look for the dimension or a stated two-per-outlet claim, and measure the gap behind your furniture and the spacing of your outlets before ordering.

faq.q: Do Eightree plugs need a hub?
faq.a: No. The SmartThings model and the Round Mini both state that no hub is required, and the others connect straight over Wi-Fi. Setup runs through the Smart Life app on the models that name it, then you link Alexa or Google Home.

faq.q: What is the usual setup mistake?
faq.a: Trying to pair a 2.4GHz-only plug, such as the Round Mini, while your phone is on 5GHz. Switch the phone to 2.4GHz for setup, or buy the dual-band 5GHz 15A model and skip the problem.

faq.q: Is the energy-monitoring plug worth it over the 5GHz 15A?
faq.a: If you want to find out what a heater or freezer costs to run, yes. Both are dual-band, but only the energy-monitoring model reports usage. For lamps and fans, the 5GHz 15A does the same job for less.

faq.q: Can I use two plugs on one outlet?
faq.a: On the energy-monitoring model, yes, since the listing says two plugs fit one outlet. The Round Mini at 1.2 inches thick should also leave room. Larger plugs may block the neighboring socket, so check your wall plate.

faq.q: Can the outdoor plug sit in rain?
faq.a: It is rated IP44, which is splash protection. Keep it under cover, such as a porch ceiling or an eave, and off the ground. For direct exposure to heavy rain, add a weatherproof outlet box.

faq.q: Will these run a space heater?
faq.a: The 5GHz 15A and Round Mini both state 15A and 1800W, which matches most heater ratings. Many heaters draw close to that limit, so check the heater label and avoid daisy-chaining. The energy-monitoring plug lists no amp rating.

finalTake: Most buyers should take the EIGHTREE 5GHz Smart Plug with Energy Monitoring: it is dual-band, certified and the only one that reports usage. The EIGHTREE 5GHz 15A is the pick for plain switching with a stated 1800W rating. Choose the SmartThings model for a Samsung home, the Outdoor plug for porch lights, and the Round Mini only for crowded outlets on a 2.4GHz network.
